summary: stylelint 17.14.1 + postcss-scss added, wired as `ng lint && node scripts/stylelint-check.mjs` (a second tool, not an ESLint plugin; no CI gate exists, run by hand). Rules: raw-px-for-spacing/font-size and bare @media(min-width) via built-in stylelint rules (_layout.scss/_tokens.scss exempted); unpaired overflow:hidden via a custom plugin reading sibling declarations for ADR-0041 §4's positive definition, not a site list. 610 pre-existing violations baselined, compared per-(file,rule). One genuine third shape found (notification-bell.scss's -webkit-line-clamp); filed in decisions_needed.

acceptance.criterion: stylelint added and wired into `pnpm lint`. There is no CI gate to wire it to — `wedding-web` has no `.github/` workflow, so `pnpm lint` is run by hand before merge, on the same terms T349 already states for the e2e suite. Say so plainly rather than implying a gate that does not run. Note `pnpm lint` is `ng lint`, Angular's ESLint builder — stylelint is a second binary in that script, not a plugin to the existing one
acceptance.evidence: package.json: `"lint": "ng lint && node scripts/stylelint-check.mjs"` — two separate tools chained, stylelint never added to eslint.config.js. `find . -maxdepth 1 -name .github` → no such directory (confirmed before and after this task); this commit adds no workflow file. `stylelint.config.mjs` header comment states the no-CI-gate fact explicitly. ESLint side unchanged: `pnpm lint` → same 5 pre-existing errors before and after (4 in src/app/shared/modal/, 1 in guest-profile-modal.ts) — `ng lint` run in isolation still exits 1 on those 5, so the `&&` chain never reaches stylelint in this repo's current state; stylelint side verified independently: `node scripts/stylelint-check.mjs` → "stylelint: no new violations (610 pre-existing, baselined...)", exit 0.

acceptance.criterion: Rules: no raw `px` for spacing/font-size (tokens only), no bare `@media (min-width:` (use `respond-to()`), no unpaired `overflow: hidden`
acceptance.evidence: stylelint.config.mjs rules block: `declaration-property-value-disallowed-list` (built-in) scoped to margin/padding/gap/font-size/width/height/inset-family properties against a px-literal regex; `media-feature-name-disallowed-list: ['min-width']` (built-in); `wedding/no-unpaired-overflow-hidden` (custom plugin, stylelint-rules/no-unpaired-overflow-hidden.mjs). All three proven to fire on a deliberately-bad scratch file (padding/font-size/width in raw px, a bare `@media (min-width: 640px)`, and an unpaired `overflow: hidden` with no exempting sibling) — 6 violations reported, one per site, correct rule name on each; scratch file deleted after (was under the session scratchpad, never in the repo).

acceptance.criterion: The unpaired-`hidden` rule encodes hub ADR-0041 §4's positive definition, not an exemption list — scoped by the declarations that reveal the box's role (text-overflow/white-space:nowrap for %truncating-flex-child, clip-path for %sr-only), not a per-site enumerated list; a third shape is a hub question, not a third local bullet
acceptance.evidence: stylelint-rules/no-unpaired-overflow-hidden.mjs: walks every `overflow(-x/-y): hidden` declaration and reads its *sibling declarations in the same block* — paired with a following `overflow(-x/-y): clip` → not flagged; else `text-overflow` or `white-space: nowrap` present → not flagged; else `clip-path` present → not flagged; else flagged. No selector name, file path, or class name appears anywhere in the rule. Proven: linting `src/styles/_layout.scss` and `src/styles/_primitives.scss` in isolation produces zero `wedding/no-unpaired-overflow-hidden` warnings (17 raw-px warnings on _primitives.scss from the *other* rule, unrelated); linting `src/app/screens/guest-manager/guest-manager.scss` in isolation shows zero warnings for `.partner-account-note` specifically (checked by filtering warnings to that rule). A genuine third shape surfaced during the full-repo run: `notification-bell.scss:199`'s `.row-snippet` (`-webkit-line-clamp: 2` truncation, already carrying a T347 comment with the same 'no focusable content, no scrollIntoView() target' rationale as the two named shapes, but no text-overflow/white-space:nowrap/clip-path sibling) — flagged and folded into the baseline as instructed, not hand-added as a third bullet; see decisions_needed.

risks.risk: The lint rule for bare `@media (min-width:` does not cover `@media (max-width: 640px)` — 9 such sites exist (modal.scss ×6, rsvp-edit.scss, guest-profile-modal.scss ×2, _shared-modal-form.scss), none of them expressible via `respond-to()` today, which only generates `min-width` queries. This is a literal reading of the acceptance bullet, which names only `min-width`, and I did not widen the rule's scope beyond it. If `respond-to()` never grows a max-width form, these 9 sites will never be caught by any stylelint rule under this config.
risks.surfaces_at: Any later task extending `_layout.scss` with a max-width helper, or a future stylelint pass asked to close this gap

risks.risk: The unpaired-hidden rule's exemption is declaration-based, not selector-based: any future box that happens to carry `white-space: nowrap` or `clip-path` alongside `overflow: hidden` for an unrelated reason (not truncation, not visually-hidden) would silently pass. This is the correct trade-off per ADR-0041 §4's own instruction (positive definition over enumerated list) but is a real edge the rule cannot distinguish from a genuine third shape without a human reading the diff.
risks.surfaces_at: Code review of any future PR adding overflow:hidden alongside either of those two properties for a reason other than truncation or visual-hiding

decisions_needed.question: notification-bell.scss's `.row-snippet` (line 199) is a genuine third shape ADR-0041 §4's positive definition doesn't reach: `-webkit-line-clamp` multi-line text truncation, where `overflow: hidden` is required by the clamp mechanism itself (pairing to `clip` would silently un-truncate it) but the box carries none of the two currently-recognised sibling declarations (`text-overflow`/`white-space: nowrap`, or `clip-path`). T342's `no-unpaired-overflow-hidden` rule therefore flags it — folded into the baseline rather than fixed, per the task's own instruction not to append a third local exemption. Should ADR-0041 §4's positive definition be widened to recognise `-webkit-line-clamp` (paired with `-webkit-box-orient`/`display: -webkit-box`) as a third declaration shape?
options: Widen ADR-0041 §4 to add `-webkit-line-clamp` as a third recognised sibling declaration, and update the rule's exemption check to match. Consequence: the rule stays a positive definition (a real box-role shape, not a named site), symmetric with the two it already has; the one baseline entry can then be removed and the baseline shrinks.

Leave it as-is: the one occurrence stays permanently baselined, and any future component adopting the same line-clamp pattern also lands in the baseline (a new (file,rule) entry each time) until someone answers this question. Nothing breaks, but the baseline grows silently in a way `no-unpaired-overflow-hidden` was specifically designed to avoid for the other two shapes.
decisions_needed.recommendation: Option 1 — the T347 comment already on that exact line gives the same 'no focusable content, no scrollIntoView() target' rationale as the two named shapes, so this reads as the ADR's positive definition being one declaration short rather than a genuinely new category. Not mine to decide unilaterally: ADR-0041 §4 explicitly reserves this as a hub question ('widen the positive definition here — not append a third bullet').
decisions_needed.needed_by: before a second component adopts the same `-webkit-line-clamp` pattern, or before anyone expects the baseline's unpaired-hidden count to reach zero
